cells.tense: Right now the stepping back and the moving forward are in the same room, and you know it.
cells.ask: Name the one thing you see holding this together, out loud, and leave it at that today.
cells.core: You can step back and catch the shape of a thing without leaving it. Not judging from a distance — just taking in what's actually there across the layers. You step back, set your direction from what you take in, and keep moving at a pace you can live with. Nothing about it feels forced. Effort and direction come from the same place, and the doing is its own reward.\n\nWhat you take in is feeding what you do next, not sitting in a notebook. So say the one thing you see keeping this steady, out loud, and let that be enough for now. Keeping it means saying it plain when you see it, and then stopping — no more than that.

cells.tense: You're already living in a version where the pattern has to hold, and you're bracing for it now.
cells.ask: Pick one piece still moving and write three lines on how it actually fits, then set the page down.
cells.core: When this is in its groove, it goes quiet: you take in the whole shape, set direction from it, and keep moving at a pace you can live with. The picture does its work and lets go. What's happening instead is you're watching for the whole pattern before it's finished, trying to hold every layer at once. What usually gives you traction has turned into a hunt for the thing that will finally make it safe. You track and cross-check so nothing catches you, and the tracking is now doing the work the stepping back used to do.\n\nMore insight won't fix this. You need enough ground to stand on while you look. See what's true so far, not all of it.

cells.tense: There was a door you walked past, and you're still standing where it used to be.
cells.ask: Go back to one ending you already moved through and name what it left you.
cells.core: You can step back from what's moving and catch the whole shape of it — what's really there across the layers, before anyone names it. Lately that step back isn't happening. You're inside the thing, reacting to what's in front of you, and the wider view doesn't come. Nothing is wrong with the view itself. The offering of it stopped somewhere back along the way.\n\nYou don't have to summon the big picture from nowhere. Go back to one ending you got through and count what it grew. Come back through that door, not around it. What you find there is yours to keep.
cells.sheetLine: You knew how to see it once. That didn't go anywhere.

cells.tense: You're already standing where the whole pattern shows, but you talk like you're still waiting to see it.
cells.ask: Say 'I saw that' about one thing you called obvious or luck, and let it be yours.
cells.core: This shows up as ordinary: you step back, catch the whole shape of a thing, and use it without ceremony. You notice what holds a thing together before anyone names it, you see across the layers, and you call it just paying attention or just being practical. The work is happening. What hasn't happened is you saying so out loud, even once. That is the whole gap — the noticing lands, the credit doesn't.\n\nYou don't have to make a case for noticing. Pick one thing you caught that turned out true — one call you made that held — and take it back. It has been yours to keep the whole time, and nobody else can say it for you.
cells.sheetLine: You already see it. You've been calling it nothing.

A reader might reasonably say 'I don't always see the whole thing; sometimes I'm just trying to get through.'
